functional_semantics.triton: out = float16(x) elementwise for a float32 1-D x, into a fresh float16 buffer; no absmax, no scale, no clamp, no integer output (impl_triton.py 13-14, 33).
functional_semantics.cutile: out = float16(x) elementwise via the DSL astype, into a fresh float16 buffer; no absmax, no scale, no clamp, no integer output (impl_cutile.py 24-25, 34).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise the reference x.to(torch.float16) (impl_torch.py 5). Verified: neither impl_torch.py nor either kernel file contains any reduction, scale factor or int8 path at this SHA; the operator is a plain fp32 -> fp16 cast despite its name. The generator always emits float32 (tensors.py 175-176) and config.yaml pins dtype to fp32 (line 9).

stages.triton: One kernel, one launch of ceil(n / tile) programs: load fp32, convert, store fp16 (impl_triton.py 8-14, 36-45).
stages.cutile: One kernel, one launch of ceil(n / tile) CTAs: load fp32, convert, store fp16 (impl_cutile.py 21-25, 53-54).
stages.note: Identical single-stage elementwise conversion; no reduction stage exists on either side.

reduction_scan_sort.triton: None; explicitly no absmax pass (impl_triton.py 8-14 is the only kernel).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: None; explicitly no absmax pass (impl_cutile.py 21-25 is the only kernel).

precision.triton: fp32 -> fp16 narrowing via the DSL cast, whose documented default is round-to-nearest-even, matching torch's .to() (impl_triton.py 14).
precision.cutile: fp32 -> fp16 narrowing via the DSL astype; the rounding mode is not stated in the source and is the library default (impl_cutile.py 25).
precision.note: Same single conversion path on both sides; the contract requires the reference's round-to-nearest-even result within config.verify tolerance. Neither side scales or clamps.

preprocessing.triton: x = x.contiguous() (no-op for the generator input); out = empty(x.shape, float16); n = x.numel() (impl_triton.py 32-34).
preprocessing.cutile: x = x.contiguous() (no-op); output = empty(x.shape, float16); n = x.numel() (impl_cutile.py 33-35).
preprocessing.note: Identical; only the output allocation and a no-op contiguity guard.

mutation.triton: x is read-only; fresh output every call (impl_triton.py 13, 33).
mutation.cutile: x is read-only; fresh output every call (impl_cutile.py 24, 34).
mutation.note: Neither side mutates the input; the contract forbids mutation.

hardware_dispatch.note: Single code path on both sides.

fq_boundary.note: With the fixed fp32 input (dtype_size = 4) the formula counts the n * 4-byte read plus the n * 2-byte float16 write, exactly what both timed run() bodies move; the contiguous() guard is a no-op and nothing is prepacked. flops_expr counts one conversion per element (config.yaml 16-17).

review_items: BLOCKING (study owner): the operator is named quantize_global but at this SHA the reference and both implementations are a plain float32 -> float16 cast with no absmax reduction, no scale factor and no integer output; decide whether to keep the operator as this cast (and rename or document it) or to redefine it as a scaled quantisation, which would require a new reference, new implementations, a new generator and a new contract. The contract below describes the cast only and must not be approved until this is settled.
